The gradient vector of a differentiable scalar-valued function at a point gives the direction of greatest increase of the function. An important type of vector field is formed by all the gradient vectors of the function (see Section 14.5). We define the gradient field of a dif- ferentiable function ƒ(x, y, z) to be the field of gradient vectors

At each point (x, y, z), the gradient field gives a vector pointing in the direction of greatest increase of ƒ, with magnitude being the value of the directional derivative in that direction. The gradient field is not always a force field or a velocity field.
